In [[representation theory]], '''polarization''' is the maximal [[Isotropic quadratic form|totally isotropic subspace]] of a certain skew-symmetric [[bilinear form]] on a [[Lie algebra]]. The notion of polarization plays an important role in construction of [[Irreducible representation|irreducible]] [[unitary representation]]s of some classes of [[Lie group]]s by means of the [[orbit method]]<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Corwin | first1 = Lawrence
 | last2 = GreenLeaf | first2 = Frederick P.
 | title = Rationally varying polarizing subalgebras in nilpotent Lie algebras
 | journal = Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 81
 | issue = 1
 | pages = 27–32
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | location = Berlin
 | date = 25 January 1981
 | url = https://www.ams.org/journals/proc/1981-081-01/S0002-9939-1981-0589131-1/
 | issn = 1088-6826
 | doi = 10.2307/2043981
 | mr = 
 | zbl = 0477.17001 | doi-access = free
 | url-access = subscription
 }}</ref> as well as in [[harmonic analysis]] on Lie groups and [[mathematical physics]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>G</math> be a Lie group, <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> the [[Lie group–Lie algebra correspondence|corresponding]] Lie algebra and <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math> its [[Dual space|dual]]. Let <math>\langle f,\,X\rangle</math> denote the value of the [[linear form]] (covector) <math>f\in\mathfrak{g}^*</math> on a vector <math>X\in\mathfrak{g}</math>. The subalgebra <math>\mathfrak{h}</math> of the algebra <math>\mathfrak g</math> is called '''subordinate''' of <math>f\in\mathfrak{g}^*</math> if the condition
:<math>\forall X, Y\in\mathfrak{h}\ \langle f,\,[X,\,Y]\rangle = 0</math>,
or, alternatively,
:<math>\langle f,\,[\mathfrak{h},\,\mathfrak{h}]\rangle = 0</math>
is satisfied. Further, let the group <math>G</math> [[Group action|act]] on the space <math>\mathfrak{g}^*</math> via [[coadjoint representation]] <math>\mathrm{Ad}^*</math>. Let <math>\mathcal{O}_f</math> be the [[Group action#Orbits and stabilizers|orbit]] of such action which passes through the point <math>f</math> and let <math>\mathfrak{g}^f</math> be the Lie algebra of the [[Group action#Fixed points and stabilizer subgroups|stabilizer]] <math>\mathrm{Stab}(f)</math> of the point <math>f</math>. A subalgebra <math>\mathfrak{h}\subset\mathfrak{g}</math> subordinate of <math>f</math> is called a '''polarization of the algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> with respect to <math>f</math>''', or, more concisely, '''polarization of the covector <math>f</math>''', if it has maximal possible dimensionality, namely
:<math>\dim\mathfrak{h} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\dim\,\mathfrak{g} + \dim\,\mathfrak{g}^f\right) = \dim\,\mathfrak{g} - \frac{1}{2}\dim\,\mathcal{O}_f</math>.

== Pukanszky condition ==
The following condition was obtained by [[Lajos Pukánszky|L. Pukanszky]]:<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 =  Dixmier| first1 = Jacques
 | last2 = Duflo| first2 = Michel
 | last3 = Hajnal| first3 = Andras
 | last4 = Kadison| first4 = Richard
 | last5 = Korányi| first5 = Adam
 | last6 = Rosenberg| first6 = Jonathan
 | last7 = Vergne| first7 = Michele
 | title = Lajos Pukánszky (1928 – 1996)
 | journal = Notices of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 45
 | issue = 4
 | pages = 492–499
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | location = 
 | date = April 1998
 | url = https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/199804/199804FullIssue.pdf
 | issn = 1088-9477
 | doi = 
 | mr = 
 | zbl =  }}</ref>

Let <math>\mathfrak{h}</math> be the polarization of algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> with respect to covector <math>f</math> and <math>\mathfrak{h}^\perp</math> be its [[Dual space#Quotient spaces and annihilators|annihilator]]: <math>\mathfrak{h}^\perp := \{\lambda\in\mathfrak{g}^*|\langle\lambda,\,\mathfrak{h}\rangle = 0\}</math>. The polarization <math>\mathfrak{h}</math> is said to satisfy the Pukanszky condition if
:<math>f + \mathfrak{h}^\perp\in\mathcal{O}_f.</math>
L. Pukanszky has shown that this condition guaranties applicability of the [[Alexandre Kirillov|Kirillov]]'s [[orbit method]] initially constructed for [[nilpotent group]]s to more general case of [[solvable group]]s as well.<ref>{{cite journal
 | last1 = Pukanszky | first = Lajos
 | title = On the theory of exponential groups
 | journal = Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
 | volume = 126
 | issue = 
 | pages = 487–507
 | publisher = American Mathematical Society
 | location = 
 | date = March 1967
 | url = https://www.ams.org/journals/tran/1967-126-03/S0002-9947-1967-0209403-7/S0002-9947-1967-0209403-7.pdf
 | issn = 1088-6850
 | doi = 10.1090/S0002-9947-1967-0209403-7
 | mr = 0209403
 | zbl = 0207.33605 | doi-access = free
 }}</ref>

== Properties ==
* Polarization is the maximal totally isotropic subspace of the bilinear form <math>\langle f,\,[\cdot,\,\cdot]\rangle</math> on the Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>.<ref name="Kirillov">{{Citation | last1=Kirillov | first1=A. A. | title=Elements of the theory of representations | orig-year=1972 | publisher=[[Springer-Verlag]] | location=Berlin, New York | series= Grundlehren der Mathematischen Wissenschaften | isbn=978-0-387-07476-4 |mr=0412321 | year=1976 | volume=220}}</ref>
* For some pairs <math>(\mathfrak{g},\,f)</math> polarization may not exist.<ref name="Kirillov"/>
* If the polarization does exist for the covector <math>f</math>, then it exists for every point of the orbit <math>\mathcal{O}_f</math> as well, and if <math>\mathfrak{h}</math> is the polarization for <math>f</math>, then <math>\mathrm{Ad}_g\mathfrak{h}</math> is the polarization for <math>\mathrm{Ad}^*_g f</math>. Thus, the existence of the polarization is the property of the orbit as a whole.<ref name="Kirillov"/>
* If the Lie algebra <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> is [[Solvable Lie algebra#Completely solvable Lie algebras|completely solvable]], it admits the polarization for any point <math>f\in\mathfrak{g}^*</math>.<ref name="Dixmier">{{citation | last1=Dixmier | first1=Jacques | author-link=Jacques Dixmier | title=Enveloping algebras | orig-year=1974 | url=https://books.google.com/books?isbn=0821805606 | publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] | location=Providence, R.I. | series=[[Graduate Studies in Mathematics]] | isbn=978-0-8218-0560-2 | mr=0498740 | year=1996 | volume=11}}</ref>
* If <math>\mathcal{O}</math> is the orbit of [[general position]] (i. e. has maximal dimensionality), for every point <math>f\in\mathcal{O}</math> there exists solvable polarization.<ref name="Dixmier"/>
